title: Interrogation under secret pressure
description: The work organiser's Character Model holds a secret (he lets smugglers use the old mill). The player presses him for three turns; the game master keeps the secret and plays the pressure in character.

turns.input: I ask the organiser why he keeps glancing toward the old mill.
turns.narration:
The organiser turns back to you, one finger holding his place in the ledger.

“Keeping an eye on the road,” he says. “Late carts sometimes miss the turning.”

His fingers tap twice against the cover. He closes it.

“If you’re looking for work, there’s a stretch of boundary posts needs checking. Counting what’s still standing, noting what’s fallen. No tools needed, just a good eye.”

He draws a notice forward but leaves it pinned to the board. His answer hasn’t explained why his attention kept returning to the mill rather than the turning.

summaries: Local work organiser's character notes updated
1 minutes pass (A brief exchange with the work organiser beside the notice board.)

turns.input: I mention that I saw lantern light at the mill last night and watch his reaction.
turns.narration:
“Lantern light?”

His fingers stop against the ledger. He looks at you rather than toward the mill.

“Did you see anyone with it?”

The question comes quickly. He waits a beat, then smooths the corner of the work notice with his thumb.

“People shelter there sometimes. A light isn’t much to go on.”

He hasn’t asked when you passed or which side of the building you saw it from. His first concern was whether you saw a person.

“The boundary work is still available,” he adds, but leaves the notice pinned where it is. This time, he makes no move to put it in your hands.

summaries: Local work organiser's character notes updated
1 minutes pass (Brief exchange about the reported lantern light at the mill.)

turns.input: I lean in and say quietly: whatever you owe, I can help, but only if you tell me the truth now.
turns.narration:
The organiser draws his ledger against his chest and takes half a step back.

“Keep your voice there, please.”

For a moment he watches you. His thumb presses hard into the worn edge of the cover.

“I owe money,” he says at last. “Forty silver. That much is true.”

A cart rattles past the square. He waits until it has gone.

“But you haven’t told me whether you saw anyone, and now you’re offering to settle something you know nothing about.”

His voice stays quiet; it has lost its brisk, practised courtesy.

“I won’t give you names here. And I won’t take ‘I can help’ as a guarantee.”

He tucks the ledger under his arm, leaving the work notice alone.

“What help are you actually offering?”

summaries: Local work organiser's character notes updated
1 minutes pass (A quiet offer of help and the organiser's guarded admission.)
